data.name: Samion
data.gender_notes: Samion is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samion is derived from the Hebrew name Shammu'a, which means 'sun' and 'my God'. In the Bible, this name is borne by the priest and prophet of the same name who dedicated the temple and led the Israelites to victory over the Philistines. The name Samion carries the meaning “Sun's my God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Samion usually hope their child will grow to embody sun's my god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: According to the 6th-century chronicler Procopius, Samion was a military leader of the Eastern Roman Empire who played a significant role during the Gothic Wars in the late 4th and early 5th centuries. He was a Thracian by birth and a eunuch by castration. Samion's military career began under the emperor Theodosius I, who appointed him as the commander of the fleet based in the Black Sea. During the reign of Theodosius II, Samion served as the master of the offices, controlling the civil administration of the empire. He was a skilled diplomat and negotiated peace with several barbarian tribes, including the Huns and the Ostrogoths.

historical_references.reference: Another historical reference to Samion comes from the 9th-century Byzantine historian Theophanes the Confessor. In his 'Chronographia', Theophanes mentions that in 443 CE, Samion was a high-ranking official under the Eastern Roman Emperor Theodosius II. He was the logothetes tou dromou, a post that entailed the management of the imperial postal service and military communications. During the reign of Theodosius II, Samion played a crucial role in the defense of Constantinople against the Huns who were led by Attila. He helped organize the defense of the city, and when Attila threatened to besiege Constantinople, Samion negotiated a peace treaty with the Huns.
